ra.mri-epilepsy.source_caption_full: Hippocampal sclerosis in a 31-year-old man with refractory right mesial temporal sclerosis. A) coronal T2-weighted image and B) coronal FLAIR images, both perpendicular to the long axis of the hippocampus. These images show a hyperintense signal, the loss of digitations and atrophy in the right hippocampal head (white arrow).

ra.mri-epilepsy.caption: One published case: A contains six selected 2D FLAIR views, B six 3D-FLAIR-derived views, and C the corresponding views with an altered display range. The article reports postoperative FCD IIb histology; that result is not inferred from MRI.
ra.mri-epilepsy.alt: FCD visibility across FLAIR presentations. One published case: A contains six selected 2D FLAIR views, B six 3D-FLAIR-derived views, and C the corresponding views with an altered display range. The article reports postoperative FCD IIb histology; that result is not inferred from MRI.
ra.mri-epilepsy.source_caption_full: A case with drug-resistant focal epilepsy, who benefited from the official standard protocol for epilepsy. It was impossible to detect any abnormalities in both coronal and axial 2D fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) images with 3-mm slice thickness (A), but the 3D FLAIR images revealed findings of a bottom-of-sulcus-type focal cortical dysplasia with transmantle sign (B), and changing the signal range is sometimes helpful to clearly visualize the lesion (C). The pathological finding was focal cortical dysplasia type IIb.
structures_visible: Source-marked focal cortical/subcortical signal and cortex-to-ventricle pattern
ra.mri-epilepsy.limits: The article reports FCD IIb from postoperative pathology; MRI does not demonstrate balloon cells or independently establish the histological subtype. Row C changes the display range of the corresponding row B images and is not a new sequence, follow-up or independent confirmation. Selected 2D views and 3D-derived views are not a released volumetric series or lesion mesh.

ra.mri-epilepsy.caption: Source-labelled left mesial temporal ganglioglioma: coronal T2 (A) shows the solid/cystic appearance and post-contrast T1 (B) shows enhancement. These are different sequences, not a pre/post-contrast T1 pair.

ra.mri-epilepsy.source_caption_full: A MRI of a ganglioglioma in a 45-year-old man with refractory left partial mesial temporal lobe epilepsy. A) A coronal T2-weighted image and B) a contrast-enhanced coronal T1-weighted image showing a solid-cystic lesion in the mesial left temporal lobe with intense enhancement of the soft tissue component (white arrows).
structures_visible: Selected solid/cystic temporal lesion and enhancing component

Complete lesion extent, native geometry and an independent diagnosis are not established.

ra.mri-epilepsy.caption: One reported familial cavernous-malformation case: coronal T2 (A) depicts larger mixed-signal lesions and their rims; axial T2-star GRE (B) depicts additional small source-described right temporal lesions. The marked lesions differ across panels.
ra.mri-epilepsy.alt: Cavernous-malformation morphology and susceptibility. One reported familial cavernous-malformation case: coronal T2 (A) depicts larger mixed-signal lesions and their rims; axial T2-star GRE (B) depicts additional small source-described right temporal lesions. The marked lesions differ across panels.
ra.mri-epilepsy.source_caption_full: Familial cerebral cavernous malformations caused by a KRIT1 gene mutation in a 36-year-old woman with multiple epileptic foci (video-EEG) and chronic partial epilepsy. A) Coronal T2-weighted images show the typical appearance of a type 2 cavernoma (white arrows) characterized by mixed signal intensity with a hemosiderin ring. B) An axial T2*-weighted gradient-echo sequence revealing two type 4 cavernomas (black arrows) in the right temporal lobe, only observed using this sequence.
structures_visible: Selected mixed-signal lesions and low-signal rims
Additional susceptibility foci on the source T2-star GRE image
ra.mri-epilepsy.limits: Panel B is T2-star GRE, not SWI. The marked lesions in B are additional source-described lesions, not registered counterparts of those marked in A. The source reports one familial case with KRIT1 mutation and multiple video-EEG foci; these images do not establish the cause of seizures, every lesion, calibrated dimensions, interval change or genetic status independently.

ra.mri-epilepsy.source_caption_full: A case with drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy and encephalocele. Constructive interference in steady-state (CISS) imaging was helpful for detection by enhancing the contrast between brain parenchyma and cerebrospinal fluid.
